title: Dolly Parton’s Official Merch Is a Reflection of the Late Singer’s Big, Bold Personality: Shop Here
summary: Since her death, fans are rushing to buy Dolly Parton merch. These official items from her store include some of the singer's best quotes.
contentText:
All products and services featured are independently chosen by editors. However, Billboard may receive a commission on orders placed through its retail links, and the retailer may receive certain auditable data for accounting purposes.

Dolly Parton ’s larger-than-life spirit has always extended far beyond her music, and her merchandise is no exception. Since the country music icon died on Aug. 25 , searches for Dolly Parton T-shirts have surged as fans look for new ways to celebrate her legacy. I recently attended Daisy Chain Fields , where I spotted plenty of festivalgoers sporting Dolly tees as a tribute to the “Jolene” singer .

The official Dolly Parton Amazon store offers plenty of ways to channel that spirit, from short- and long-sleeve shirts to sweatshirts and hoodies in a variety of colors and sizes for both children and adults. You’ll also find hats and tote bags featuring designs that capture Dolly’s wit, music and passions along with imagery spanning her remarkable seven-decade career.

If you thought Dolly Parton’s official merchandise stopped at clothing, think again. The collection reaches well beyond apparel, with everything from PopSockets and cast iron cookware to beauty products , books and calendars and planners .

Holiday shoppers can also find festive Dolly-themed pieces, including a “Holly Dolly Christmas” cushion . Her love of animals is represented, too, through the Doggy Parton pet line inspired by the singer’s signature style. Better yet, a portion of proceeds supports Willa B. Farms animal sanctuary in Tennessee, which cares for rescued and displaced animals.

Sophie Dunne  is an e-commerce writer at Penske Media Corporation, writing across Billboard, The Hollywood Reporter, Rolling Stone, WWD, and Footwear News. Originally from Ireland and based in Los Angeles, she previously worked at Static Media as a writer and editor, covering entertainment, lifestyle, fashion, and travel. Her bylines have appeared in Women’s Health, The List, Women.com, Islands, Grunge, WebMD, and more. Before beginning her writing career in 2019, Sophie lived in Dubai for four years working as an Emirates cabin crew member. Having traveled to 71 countries with the airline, she began writing for an LA-based publication as a travel writer during her final year. Sophie has a degree in Humanities from Carlow College, St. Patrick’s (now South East Technological University) in her native Ireland. She studied English, history, philosophy, and psychology. Sophie mostly reports on entertainment merchandise and celebrity brand partnerships.
